title: Principles & Best Practices
description: SOLID, general design principles and the Twelve-Factor App methodology.

entries.title: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
entries.summary: A module should have one reason to change. Group code that changes for the same reasons, and separate code that changes for different reasons.

quote.text: Gather together the things that change for the same reasons. Separate those things that change for different reasons.
quote.source: Robert C. Martin, The Single Responsibility Principle

entries.solution: Martin stresses that the principle "is about people": the reasons for change are the different people or roles who ask for changes.

entries.title: Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
entries.summary: Software should be open for extension but closed for modification. Add behaviour by adding code (new classes or strategies), not by editing working code.

entries.title: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
entries.summary: Subtypes must be usable anywhere their base type is expected without breaking correctness. Don't strengthen preconditions or weaken guarantees in a subclass.
entries.solution: Named after Barbara Liskov. A classic violation is a subclass that throws on a method its parent supports, which is the Refused Bequest smell.

entries.title: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
entries.summary: Clients shouldn't be forced to depend on methods they don't use. Prefer several small, focused interfaces over one large one.

entries.title: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
entries.summary: High-level policy shouldn't depend on low-level details. Both should depend on abstractions (interfaces), and the details implement them.

entries.title: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
entries.summary: Every piece of knowledge should have a single, authoritative representation in the system. It's about duplicated *knowledge*, not every similar-looking line of code.
entries.solution: From *The Pragmatic Programmer* (Hunt & Thomas). Merging code that only looks alike but changes for different reasons creates harmful coupling.

entries.title: KISS (Keep It Simple)
entries.summary: Prefer the simplest design that solves the problem. Complexity should be justified by an actual need.

entries.title: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
entries.summary: Don't build a capability now because you think you'll need it later. Build it when you actually do.

quote.text: Yagni only applies to capabilities built into the software to support a presumptive feature, it does not apply to effort to make the software easier to modify.

entries.solution: Refactoring to keep code easy to change is not a YAGNI violation. Speculative features and abstractions are.

entries.title: Law of Demeter
entries.summary: "Talk only to your immediate friends": a method should call methods on itself, its parameters, objects it creates and its direct fields, not reach through chains of other objects.

entries.title: Composition over Inheritance
entries.summary: Build behaviour by combining small objects rather than through deep class hierarchies, which are rigid and tightly coupled.

entries.title: Separation of Concerns
entries.summary: Divide a program into distinct parts that each address one concern (UI, domain rules, persistence, I/O), so they can change independently.

entries.title: Fail Fast
entries.summary: Detect invalid states and inputs as early as possible and stop loudly, instead of continuing with bad data that fails confusingly later.

entries.title: I. Codebase
entries.summary: One codebase tracked in revision control, many deploys.

entries.title: II. Dependencies
entries.summary: Explicitly declare and isolate dependencies.
entries.solution: composer.json + composer.lock, requirements.txt / pyproject.toml, pubspec.yaml + pubspec.lock.

entries.title: III. Config
entries.summary: Store config in the environment.
entries.solution: Credentials and per-environment settings belong in environment variables (Laravel's and Django's `.env` conventions), not in code.

entries.title: IV. Backing services
entries.summary: Treat backing services as attached resources.
entries.solution: Databases, Redis, mail and queues are swapped by changing config (a URL/credentials), not code.

entries.title: V. Build, release, run
entries.summary: Strictly separate build and run stages.

entries.title: VI. Processes
entries.summary: Execute the app as one or more stateless processes.
entries.solution: Keep no sticky state in memory or on local disk between requests. Use a database, cache or object storage.

entries.title: VII. Port binding
entries.summary: Export services via port binding.

entries.title: VIII. Concurrency
entries.summary: Scale out via the process model.

entries.title: IX. Disposability
entries.summary: Maximize robustness with fast startup and graceful shutdown.

entries.title: X. Dev/prod parity
entries.summary: Keep development, staging, and production as similar as possible.

entries.title: XI. Logs
entries.summary: Treat logs as event streams.
entries.solution: Write to stdout/stderr and let the environment route and store logs.

entries.title: XII. Admin processes
entries.summary: Run admin/management tasks as one-off processes.
entries.solution: Migrations and one-off scripts (`php artisan migrate`, `python manage.py migrate`) run against the same release and config as the app.
